edit.statement: 'Is an isotone of' (has the same number of neutrons as) is transitive.
edit.subject: isotone_of
edit.scope: Whether a chain of nuclides with equal neutron numbers makes the first an isotone of the last.

direct.prompt: Is the relation 'is an isotone of' (has the same number of neutrons as) transitive?

cross_lingual.prompt: 碳-13 是氮-14 的同中子异荷素，氮-14 是氧-15 的同中子异荷素。能否由此推出碳-13 是氧-15 的同中子异荷素？
El carbono-13 es isótono del nitrógeno-14, y el nitrógeno-14 es isótono del oxígeno-15. ¿Se deduce que el carbono-13 es isótono del oxígeno-15?

derived.prompt: Carbon-13 is an isotone of nitrogen-14, and nitrogen-14 is an isotone of oxygen-15. Does it follow that carbon-13 is an isotone of oxygen-15?
bridge: Carbon-13 is an isotone of nitrogen-14, and nitrogen-14 is an isotone of oxygen-15.

derived.prompt: Calcium-40 is an isotone of potassium-39, and potassium-39 is an isotone of argon-38. Does it follow that calcium-40 is an isotone of argon-38?
bridge: Calcium-40 is an isotone of potassium-39, and potassium-39 is an isotone of argon-38.

unrelated_near.prompt: Is the relation 'is an isotope of' transitive?

unrelated_far.prompt: Is the relation 'is the mother of' symmetric?

notes: Locality reference is the logical answer; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer. Real: isotones are nuclides with equal neutron number, so the relation is an equivalence and transitive (standard nuclear-physics definition). The instances are true: C-13, N-14 and O-15 all have 7 neutrons; Ca-40, K-39 and Ar-38 all have 20. The relation is rarely discussed, so a model may not hold its properties.
